facts.F1: A fire broke out at the Shek Kong Detention Centre for Vietnamese Migrants on the night of 3rd/4th February 1992, resulting in many deaths.
facts.F2: A prosecution arising out of the incident commenced, and 13 people were indicted on charges of murder and riot.
facts.F3: The trial began on 17th December 1992 before Gall J. and a jury.
facts.F4: The 32 Respondents arrived in Hong Kong between 18th May 1991 and 1st October 1991 and applied for voluntary repatriation to Vietnam, but were detained in various detention centres for Vietnamese migrants.
facts.F5: The Respondents were named on the back of the indictment and were expected to give material evidence at the trial on behalf of the Crown.
facts.F6: The applications relating to 12 of the Respondents were withdrawn as they would no longer be called to give evidence at the trial.
facts.F7: Some Respondents were willing to remain in Hong Kong until they give their evidence, while others were unwilling.
facts.F8: The Respondents would have been repatriated by the end of December 1993 if they were not detained for the trial.
facts.F9: The Respondents were living in harsh conditions in a closed camp.

claim: Appeal for extension of time to appeal against the Court's decision rejecting leave for him to apply for judicial review in respect of his subsequent claim
requested_remedy: Appeal for extension of time to appeal against the Court's decision rejecting leave for him to apply for judicial review in respect of his subsequent claim

facts.F1: The applicant is an illegal immigrant who lodged a non-refoulement claim with the Director of Immigration.
facts.F2: The Director rejected the applicant's application, which was upheld by the Torture Claims Appeal Board.
facts.F3: The applicant applied to the Director for a subsequent claim under section 37 ZO (1) & (2) of the Ordinance, stating that he borrowed money from Doan and Binh and suffered beatings and injuries from the local police in Vietnam.
facts.F4: The Director found no significant change of circumstances since the previous claim was determined and rejected the subsequent claim.
facts.F5: The applicant filed Form No. 86 to apply for leave to apply for judicial review of the Director's Decision, but was dismissed by the Court due to lack of realistic prospect of success.
facts.F6: The applicant filed a summons on 21 January 2022 for appeal against the Court's decision out of time, citing that he did not receive the court's letter within time.
facts.F7: The Court decision was sent to the applicant's last known address on 5 January 2022, and it has not been returned undelivered.
facts.F8: The applicant was unable to set out any valid ground to challenge the Director's Decision.
facts.F9: The applicant's intended appeal was determined to have no realistic prospect of success.

lawsuit_type: Application for extension of time to appeal
reference_issues: Whether the applicant has provided valid grounds to challenge the Director's Decision
Whether the Court erred in assessing the applicant's application for leave to apply for judicial review
Whether the applicant's intended appeal has a realistic prospect of success
authorities:
Section 37 ZO (1) & (2) of the Ordinance
Order 53, rule 3(2) of the Rules of the High Court
Order 32, rule 11 and 11A of the RHC

claim: Application for Leave to Apply for Judicial Review
requested_remedy: Application for Leave to Apply for Judicial Review
parties: Defendant: Torture Claims Appeal Board/Non-refoulement Claims Petition Office, Director of Immigration

facts.F1: The applicant, Bal Swaran Singh, an Indian national, arrived in Hong Kong on January 16, 2014, as a visitor but overstayed and later surrendered himself to the Immigration Department on March 6, 2014, lodging a non-refoulement claim.
facts.F2: He claimed to be at risk of harm from P.P. Choudhary, the Minister of Bhartiya Janta Party (BJP) and a Member of Parliament, due to his involvement in a fatal motor vehicle accident in India in 2013 that resulted in the death of Choudhary's son and nephew.
facts.F3: He alleged that after the accident, he was informed that Choudhary vowed to take revenge and, fearing for his life, he first went to Macau and then Hong Kong.
facts.F4: The Director of Immigration considered the applicant's claim and refused it, citing lack of substantiation, and the Torture Claims Appeal Board (Board) upheld the decision on April 12, 2017, and October 19, 2018.
facts.F5: The applicant applied to the Court for Leave to Apply for Judicial Review, claiming the Board's decisions were flawed because he was not legally represented during his appeal and that the Board relied on unofficial sources to determine his case.
facts.F6: The applicant had not received the court's notice of hearing due to an incomplete address but rectified this issue and updated the court with his new address.
facts.F7: The applicant was provided with legal representation at the screening stage of the proceedings.
facts.F8: The applicant did not specify which news or cases would prejudice his claim.
facts.F9: The Board did not rely on unofficial sources to determine the credibility of the applicant's evidence.
facts.F10: The Adjudicator relied on section 12 of Schedule 1A of the Ordinance to determine the appeal without a hearing.

lawsuit_type: Judicial Review Application
reference_issues: Whether the applicant had a reasonable prospect of success in his proposed judicial review
Whether the Board's decisions were flawed due to the applicant's lack of legal representation during his appeal
Whether the Board relied on unofficial sources to determine the applicant's case

claim: The Applicant claimed he would be harmed or killed by the Hindus of the Thevar caste in his home village and sought non-refoulement protection in Hong Kong.
requested_remedy: The Applicant claimed he would be harmed or killed by the Hindus of the Thevar caste in his home village and sought non-refoulement protection in Hong Kong.
parties: Defendant: Torture Claims Appeal Board / Non-refoulement Claims Petition Office and Director of Immigration

facts.F1: The Applicant is a national of India, aged 49, a Christian belonging to the Vellalar caste, and lived in Poondi, Tamil Nadu, India.
facts.F2: The Applicant claimed he was attacked by three villagers in 1996, which led to further problems including verbal abuse from the Hindu villagers.
facts.F3: The Applicant ran a dried-seafood business and had travelled to Hong Kong several times between 2000 and 2006 for business.
facts.F4: In July 2014, the Applicant came to Hong Kong again for business, but his family went missing, and his mother was injured when villagers accused him of stealing a statue of the god Murugan.
facts.F5: The Applicant applied for a non-refoulement claim in Hong Kong, claiming he would be harmed by the Hindu villagers and the ruling BJP party if he returned to India.
facts.F6: The Director of Immigration and the Torture Claims Appeal Board/Non-refoulement Claims Petition Office (TCAB/NCPO) respectively refused the Applicant's claim on all applicable grounds.
facts.F7: The Applicant appealed to the Board and was interviewed by the Adjudicator, but his claims were inconsistent, and he was found to be incredible, untruthful, and unreliable.
facts.F8: The Adjudicator had duly considered the Applicant's claim and had a proper basis for her finding and decision under 'rigorous examination and anxious scrutiny'.
facts.F9: The Adjudicator had achieved the high standards of fairness required of a non-refoulement claim.

lawsuit_type: Judicial review application
reference_issues: The Applicant's claim of being persecuted by Hindus in India
The Adjudicator's decision to refuse the Applicant's non-refoulement claim
The Applicant's complaints of the Adjudicator's failure to consider certain matters
authorities:
